extracted.intended_audience: Investigators and others preparing or reviewing protocols for randomised trials (investigators, trial teams, funders, research ethics committees, journals, trial registries, policymakers, regulators, and reviewers).
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing complete, transparent protocols for randomized controlled trials using the SPIRIT 2025 minimum-item checklist and accompanying materials. Focuses on which items must be addressed in a protocol and how to present schedule/intervention information.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPIRIT 2025 minimum-item checklist (34 items)
rubrics_metrics.description: The updated SPIRIT 2025 statement consists of an evidence-based checklist of 34 minimum items to address in a trial protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist defines the minimum content that should appear in a randomised trial protocol; an expanded version and an explanation and elaboration document were developed to facilitate implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and transparency of protocol content
rubrics_metrics.description: The protocol is the foundation for study planning, conduct, reporting, and external review; protocols vary in completeness and often do not address key elements of design and conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocols should address all key elements of design and conduct to improve transparency and completeness for the benefit of investigators, participants, funders, ethics committees, journals, registries, policymakers, regulators, and other reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open science practices (new open science section)
rubrics_metrics.description: The updated guidance includes a new open science section to be included in trial protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the abstract does not list specific open-science items, the inclusion indicates protocols should describe open science plans (e.g., data sharing, access to protocols/analysis code). Implementers should consult the expanded checklist and E&E document for specific expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and reporting of harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional emphasis on the assessment of harms is included in SPIRIT 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocols should prespecify how harms will be assessed and reported; SPIRIT 2025 also integrates key items from CONSORT/Harms extensions. See expanded checklist/E&E for detailed items and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description of interventions and comparators
rubrics_metrics.description: SPIRIT 2025 places additional emphasis on the description of interventions and comparators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrates relevant items from TIDieR and CONSORT extensions to ensure interventions and comparators are described sufficiently for replication and interpretation (e.g., content, timing, mode of delivery, fidelity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient and public involvement (PPI)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new item on how patients and the public will be involved in trial design, conduct, and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocols should describe plans for patient and public involvement across design, conduct, and dissemination, including roles, methods of engagement, and how PPI influenced protocol decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of enrolment, interventions, and assessments (diagram)
rubrics_metrics.description: The updated statement includes a diagram illustrating the schedule of enrolment, interventions, and assessments for trial participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended content can be displayed using various schematic formats. Guidance examples: 'List target time points and acceptable time windows in this row (e.g., 30 ± 3 days).' Use arrows to indicate continuous delivery (e.g., drug) and discrete timepoint notation for comparators (e.g., psychotherapy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of items from other reporting guidelines and CONSORT extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: SPIRIT 2025 integrates key items from other relevant reporting guidelines and CONSORT extensions (Harms, Outcomes, Non-pharmacological Treatment) and TIDieR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing protocols, include items recommended by related guidance (e.g., detailed outcome definitions, harms reporting, non-pharmacological treatment specifics, TIDieR items for intervention description) to ensure completeness and harmonization with reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based update and consensus-derived modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The update was produced via scoping review, creation of a project-specific evidence database, Delphi ratings, and a consensus meeting leading to additions, revisions, deletions/mergers, and integrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol authors and reviewers should treat SPIRIT 2025 as an evidence- and consensus-informed minimum standard; changes from SPIRIT 2013 include two new items, revision to five items, deletion/merger of five items, and integration of other guideline items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of expanded checklist and explanation & elaboration (E&E) for implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: An expanded version of the SPIRIT 2025 checklist and an accompanying explanation and elaboration document were developed to facilitate implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the expanded checklist and E&E for item-level examples, fuller descriptions, and implementation advice when drafting or reviewing protocols; these documents provide scoring/interpretation details and illustrative examples beyond the concise minimum checklist.
